Use Python to inspect the evidence, refine that world model from the newest history, and search or score candidate actions or short sequences against the current goal as you currently understand it.
Maintain a compact working world model of what the current level seems to contain, what actions appear to do, what the goal seems to be, what is still uncertain, and what plan currently looks best.

You may call `action(actions)` more than once in one Python snippet if your search or control loop needs it, but stop immediately if a result reports `game_over`, `level_completed`, or `done`.
Working world model carried from earlier turns:
- World model: - The level consists of a large background of `b` (blue) with a vertical stripe of `S` (sky blue) near the right edge, and a column of `B` (black) at the far right. - There are several distinct object groups: * A large rectangular block of `B` (black) at the far right edge. * A central structure of `B`/`W`/`c`/`p` etc (the “puzzle area”) that contains colored patterns (yellow `Y` rows, orange `O`, etc.) and a repeating pattern of `B`/`W`/`c`/`p`. * The yellow `Y` rows form a horizontal band near the bottom of the puzzle area. - Actions observed: * `ACTION7` shifts the whole puzzle area left by one column (observed multiple times). * `SPACE` toggles a single cell (likely a cursor or selector) but does not affect the main puzzle. * Arrow keys move the puzzle area up/down/left/right by one cell (observed `DOWN` moving the yellow band down). - Goal appears to be to align the yellow band with the black column on the far right (or to move the puzzle area so that the yellow band reaches the right edge), which likely triggers level completion.
- Recent findings: - Repeated `ACTION7` moves the puzzle left; repeated `DOWN` moves the yellow band down. - The yellow band is currently at the bottom but not yet aligned with the black column. - No progress after further `DOWN` or `SPACE`; likely need to move the puzzle area rightwards to bring the yellow band into contact with the black column.
- Open questions: - How to move the puzzle area right? Arrow `RIGHT` may shift the whole area rightwards. - Does aligning the yellow band with the black column complete the level?
- Plan: - Try moving the puzzle area right until the yellow band contacts the black column. Use a short batch of `RIGHT` actions. Action: ```python action(['RIGHT','RIGHT','RIGHT','RIGHT','RIGHT'], intent='solve') ```
- Revise any item above immediately if `current_frame` or `history` contradicts it.
end of world model.

If you include assistant text before a tool call, keep it short and use it to update the world model. Helpful optional prefixes are `World model:`, `Goal model:`, `Action model:`, `Recent findings:`, `Open questions:`, `Plan:`, and `Cross-level notes:`.
When calling `python`, emit exactly the tool-call format shown elsewhere in this prompt for this model. Use only that format; do not add markdown fences, prose wrappers, or alternate tool-call syntax. Do not quote or place tool-call markup inside explanatory text; when you decide to call the tool, emit the tool call itself.
If you use MOUSE, include integer row and col arguments.
EFFICIENCY BUDGET — your score on each level is (baseline_actions / your_actions)^2, so every wasted action costs you quadratically.
Level 1: you have used 59 actions; a strong score needs about 32 or fewer. You are 1.8x over the target.
If you are not steadily making progress toward the level goal, commit to your single best hypothesis and the shortest sequence that tests it — do not exhaustively scan rows/columns or enumerate every option. Test one idea, read the result, then decide.
